title: ICE Agent Shoots Venezuelan DoorDash Driver in Austin; Shooting Agent Not Wearing Assigned Camera
excerpt: An ICE officer shot and seriously wounded 28-year-old Venezuelan asylum seeker Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez while he was making a food delivery in North Austin, Texas. The shooting agent had been issued a body camera but was not wearing it — the latest in a pattern of ICE shootings with limited video accountability.
content:
On September 20, 2026, an ICE officer shot Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan man and DoorDash delivery driver, in North Austin, Texas. Garcés Pérez was shot in the torso, with a bullet lodging in his back, and was transported to Dell Seton Medical Center in serious but stable condition.

  • Attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch identified her client as an asylum seeker who entered the U.S. through the CBP One parole program, with no criminal history and two years of residence in Austin.
  • The ICE officer who fired was a recent recruit who had been issued a body camera but was not wearing it during the shooting, according to two DHS officials who spoke to NBC News. Another officer at the scene wore a camera but captured only partial footage that did not include the moment of the shooting.
  • DHS stated the man had a final order of removal and that the shooting followed a "dangerous attempt to evade arrest" during a foot pursuit. Garcés Pérez's attorney disputed parts of this account.
  • Four hours after being shot and discharged from the hospital, Garcés Pérez was transferred directly to ICE custody at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall — before his family knew his location. He later required rehospitalization for significant pain and a bullet still lodged in his side.
  • The Travis County District Attorney's Office sent a letter to DHS and ICE requesting that Garcés Pérez remain in the country as a "material witness" in their criminal investigation of the shooting.
  • A federal judge issued an emergency order temporarily blocking his deportation.
  • The incident was described as at least the third ICE-linked shooting of a person in Texas since Trump's second term, part of a national count of approximately 20 or more people shot by ICE and CBP agents.

More than 100 protesters gathered at the shooting scene. Rep. Greg Casar called it "a disturbing pattern" that must stop. The shooting renewed congressional calls to mandate body cameras and release footage publicly.
